title: Legal actions. Paired experiments. Defensible decisions.
summary: An agent-research project connecting legal observations, resource allocation, policy integration, and evidence-based promotion. The public lab exposes the mechanics behind policy behavior without distributing private competition strategies.

signals.label: Recorded development and later holdout episodes

scope: The Python checks validate published sprint evidence and execute the authored action-contract example. Optional Node tests exercise the farming lab. The lab is a simplified synthetic economy, not the official simulator or a claimed deployed policy.
private_boundary: Raw episode logs, private feature matrices, exact strategy parameters, competition checkpoints, opponent-specific state, and unpublished policy recipes remain excluded.

cards.title: Constrain the agent to legal information and actions.
cards.decision: Connect observable state to feasible actions instead of allowing hidden simulator state to enter the policy.
cards.boundary: The public example illustrates contracts, not competitive strength.

cards.title: Evaluate policies on paired populations.
cards.decision: Separate development from a later holdout and preserve the registered promotion decision.
cards.boundary: Local returns and synthetic lab outcomes are not official ranking estimates.

cards.title: Reuse completed experiments rather than replay games.
cards.decision: Track accepted results and artifact identities so expensive completed episodes remain reusable.
cards.boundary: Reuse establishes execution efficiency, not a new policy improvement.

cards.title: Separate scientific failure from transport failure.
cards.decision: Record failed promotions and post-game diagnostics as different events in the review evidence.
cards.boundary: A successfully executed negative experiment is not a better policy.
